proposals.before: She died in the tenth month. Taizu mourned at her residence in person, suspended court for five days, and gave her the posthumous epithet Gongyi.
proposals.after: She died in the tenth month. Taizu came in person to mourn, suspended court for five days, and gave her the posthumous epithet Gongyi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 臨哭 means he came in person to wail or mourn; the idiomatic version invents a residence not stated in this sentence.

proposals.before: Under Emperor Zhenzong she was raised to Grand Princess.
proposals.after: Under Emperor Zhenzong she was raised to Senior Princess.
proposals.reason: Chinese 進長公主 is the rank 長公主, not 大長公主 (Grand Princess).

proposals.before: Under Zhenzong, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
proposals.after: Under Zhenzong, she was advanced to Senior Princess.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長公主 is mistranslated as Grand Princess, which corresponds to 大長公主.

proposals.before: Early in Emperor Zhenzong's reign she was raised to Grand Princess.
proposals.after: Early in Emperor Zhenzong's reign she was raised to Senior Princess.
proposals.reason: Chinese 進長公主 is not 大長公主; the next sentence then advances her further to 大長公主.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Zhenzong, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Zhenzong, she was advanced to Senior Princess.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長公主 is mistranslated as Grand Princess.

proposals.before: Early in Emperor Zhenzong's reign she was raised to Princess of Xu.
proposals.after: Early in Emperor Zhenzong's reign she was raised to Senior Princess of Xu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許國長公主 includes the rank 長公主 omitted in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: The Grand Princess of the State of Bin, in the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo became a nun, with the style name Master Yuanming.
proposals.after: The Grand Princess of the State of Bin, in the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo became a nun, with the religious name Master Yuanming.
proposals.reason: Chinese 號 here marks a Buddhist religious name, not a courtesy or style name.

proposals.before: Once, when Li Zunxu was posted to Xuzhou and fell suddenly ill, the princess was desperate to rush to his side. Her attendants said she must petition the throne and await approval before leaving; she set out without waiting, accompanied by only five or six people.
proposals.after: Once, when Li Zunxu was posted to Xu Prefecture and fell suddenly ill, the princess was desperate to rush to his side. Her attendants said she must petition the throne and await approval before leaving; she set out without waiting, accompanied by only five or six people.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu Prefecture (modern Xuchang), not 徐州 Xuzhou; the idiomatic rendering conflates the two place names.

proposals.before: At first, when Zunxu went out to govern Xuzhou and suddenly fell ill, the Princess urgently wished to hurry to see him; attendants reported that one must memorialize and receive a reply before going; the Princess did not wait for the reply and went, with only five or six followers.
proposals.after: At first, when Zunxu went out to govern Xu Prefecture and suddenly fell ill, the Princess urgently wished to hurry to see him; attendants reported that one must memorialize and receive a reply before going; the Princess did not wait for the reply and went, with only five or six followers.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 許州 as Xuzhou, which names a different prefecture (徐州).

proposals.before: On another occasion she slipped while bathing a servant's quarters and hurt her right arm. The emperor sent a eunuch to punish her attendants, but she said, "My strength has failed early; I can scarcely walk—this is no fault of those around me."
proposals.after: On another occasion she slipped while bathing and fell to the ground, hurting her right arm. The emperor sent a eunuch to punish her attendants, but she said, "My strength has failed early; I can scarcely walk—this is no fault of those around me."
proposals.reason: Chinese 浴僕地 means she fell to the ground (僕地) while bathing; the English invents servant's quarters by misreading 僕.

proposals.before: Once when she slipped while bathing in the servants' quarters and injured her right arm, the Emperor sent a palace eunuch to rebuke the attendants; the Princess said, "I am early failing in strength and cannot manage walking—this is not the fault of those beside me."
proposals.after: Once when she slipped while bathing and fell to the ground and injured her right arm, the Emperor sent a palace eunuch to rebuke the attendants; the Princess said, "I am early failing in strength and cannot manage walking—this is not the fault of those beside me."
proposals.reason: Literal English also misreads 僕地 as servants' quarters rather than falling to the ground.

proposals.before: The Grand Princess of Sheng first took Buddhist orders.
proposals.after: The Grand Princess of Sheng first took Daoist orders.
proposals.reason: 入道 with the later Daoist religious name 清虛靈照大師 is Daoist ordination, not Buddhist.

proposals.before: In the second year of Mingdao, she was enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Wei, with the style name Master Qingxu Lingzhao.
proposals.after: In the second year of Mingdao, she was enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Wei, with the religious name Master Qingxu Lingzhao.
proposals.reason: 號 here is a religious name, not a courtesy/style name.

proposals.before: In 1057 she was promoted to Princess of the State of Yan.
proposals.after: In 1057 she was promoted to Princess of the State of Gun.
proposals.reason: Chinese 袞國 is Gun, not Yan (兗).

proposals.before: In the second year of Jiayou, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Yan.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jiayou, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Gun.
proposals.reason: Chinese 袞國 is Gun, not Yan.

proposals.before: After a long time, Wei was again summoned and made Commissioner-in-Ordinary Attached to the Palace as before.
proposals.after: After a long time, Wei was again summoned and made Commandant-escort (imperial son-in-law) as before.
proposals.reason: 附馬都尉 is 駙馬都尉, the imperial son-in-law office, not a palace commissioner-in-ordinary.

proposals.before: Twenty-nine years later, Mingyi was added to her posthumous title.
proposals.after: In the twenty-ninth year, Mingyi was added to her posthumous title.
proposals.reason: 二十九年 is a regnal year (Shaoxing 29), not an elapsed span of twenty-nine years.

proposals.before: The Grand Princess of Yan was the emperor's eleventh daughter.
proposals.after: The Grand Princess of Gun was the emperor's eleventh daughter.
proposals.reason: 袞國 is Gun, not Yan (燕); the idiomatic rendering confuses the fief.

proposals.before: The Grand Princess of the State of Yan was the Emperor's eleventh daughter.
proposals.after: The Grand Princess of the State of Gun was the Emperor's eleventh daughter.
proposals.reason: The source title is 袞國, which is Gun, not Yan.

proposals.before: In the summer of her tenth year, during a drought, the Cao clan prepared a lavish birthday feast; she said, "The court is cutting back meals and suspending music—how could I enjoy such a celebration?"
proposals.after: In the summer of the tenth year, during a drought, the Cao clan prepared a lavish birthday feast; she said, "The court is cutting back meals and suspending music—how could I enjoy such a celebration?"
proposals.reason: 十年 continues the preceding 熙甯九年 and means the tenth year of Xining, not the princess's tenth year of age.

proposals.before: Huizong posthumously made her Princess of Yan and later retitled her Grand Imperial Princess Xianyi Gongmu.
proposals.after: Huizong posthumously made her Princess of Gun and later retitled her Grand Imperial Princess Xianyi Gongmu.
proposals.reason: 追封袞國 is Gun, not Yan.

proposals.before: When Shenzong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Shu, redesignated Princess of Shu, and married Wang Shen, a general of the Left Guard.
proposals.after: When Shenzong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Shu (舒), redesignated Princess of Shu (蜀), and married Wang Shen, a general of the Left Guard.
proposals.reason: 舒國 and 蜀國 are successive distinct titles collapsed into the same English 'Shu'.

proposals.before: During mourning for Empress Cisheng Guangxian, when the emperor was utterly prostrate with grief, she said, "We are of one flesh—how can I alone find comfort in music!"
proposals.after: During mourning for Empress Cisheng Guangxian, when the emperor was utterly prostrate with grief, she said, "We are of one flesh—how can I alone remain at ease in this!"
proposals.reason: 保聊 does not mention music; the idiomatic line invents a musical comfort absent from the Chinese.

proposals.before: She received the title Denning.
proposals.after: She received the title Dening.
proposals.reason: 德寧 is Dening; Denning is an English misspelling.

proposals.before: From birth she was quick-witted; from childhood in restraint her tastes and habits were like an adult's.
proposals.after: From birth she was quick-witted; from the bound-hair years of childhood her tastes and habits were like an adult's.
proposals.reason: 羈丱 names the childhood hair-binding stage, not moral restraint; the literal rendering 'in restraint' misreads the age term.

proposals.before: She bore another son, who did not survive and died; a concubine of Teng bore a daughter, whom she reared and regarded as her own.
proposals.after: She bore another son, who did not survive and died; a concubine bore a daughter, whom she reared and regarded as her own.
proposals.reason: 滕妾 here is a concubine (commonly 媵妾); 'concubine of Teng' treats 滕 as a surname the sentence does not establish.

proposals.before: Princess of Qin, posthumously Kangyi, was the emperor's third daughter.
proposals.after: Princess of Qin Kangyi was the emperor's third daughter.
proposals.reason: 始封康懿 shows Kangyi is her first title, not a posthumous name; the idiomatic 'posthumously' is invented.

proposals.before: Pan Zhengfu has served four reigns. At Bianjing he urged welcoming Your Majesty; at Hangzhou he warned that the palace guard was not yet assembled and that unrest should be guarded against. I beg that he be granted the office of Grand Preceptor of the Palace."
proposals.after: Pan Zhengfu has served four reigns. At Bianjing he urged welcoming Your Majesty; at Hangzhou he warned that the palace guard was not yet assembled and that unrest should be guarded against. I beg that he be granted kaifu (the privilege of opening an office)."
proposals.reason: 開府 is the kaifu privilege, not Grand Preceptor (太師/太傅).

proposals.before: It was extremely hot; the Emperor each time dressed formally to dine with her, and again sought favors for Zhengfu. The Emperor said, "How can offices and ranks be given privately to others? Moreover, today there are many affairs, and there is no leisure for this."
proposals.after: It was extremely hot; the Emperor each time dressed formally to dine with her, and she again sought favors for Zhengfu. The Emperor said, "How can offices and ranks be given privately to others? Moreover, today there are many affairs, and there is no leisure for this."
proposals.reason: 又為正夫求恩數 has the princess as subject, not the emperor.

proposals.before: After Ding left office, Zhengfu finally received appointment as Grand Preceptor of the Palace.
proposals.after: After Ding left office, Zhengfu finally received the kaifu appointment.
proposals.reason: 開府之命 is the kaifu appointment, not Grand Preceptor of the Palace.

proposals.before: Roufu died in 1141; when the imperial coffin procession returned, her remains were brought back, interred, and she was posthumously made Princess of He.
proposals.after: Roufu died in 1141; when the imperial coffin procession returned, her remains were brought back, interred, and she was posthumously made Grand Princess of the State of He.
proposals.reason: 和國長公主 is a senior/grand princess title, not merely Princess of He.

proposals.before: In April 1261, because Empress Dowager Yang had helped place him on the throne, the emperor chose her grandnephew Zhen as the princess's consort.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of 1261, because Empress Dowager Yang had helped place him on the throne, the emperor chose her grandnephew Zhen as the princess's consort.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 四月 is a lunar month, not the Gregorian month April; the idiomatic rendering invents a Western calendar month.

proposals.before: Members of Zhen's clan and his wife's sisters were all promoted and ennobled—the favor shown them was extraordinary.
proposals.after: Members of Zhen's clan and his brothers' wives were all promoted and ennobled—the favor shown them was extraordinary.
proposals.reason: 娣姒 denotes sisters-in-law as wives of brothers, not the wife's own sisters.

decisions.reason: 臨哭 means Taizu came in person to mourn; this sentence does not name a residence, so “at her residence” is invented.
進長公主 is the rank 長公主 (Senior Princess), not 大長公主; Yuanfu later makes her 魏國大長公主.
The Chinese is 長公主, which this translation system renders as Senior Princess; Grand Princess is 大長公主.
真宗初，進長公主 is Senior Princess; the next sentence 進大長公主 is the further rise to Grand Princess.
Literal English likewise renders 長公主 as Grand Princess, which belongs to 大長公主 in the following sentence.
許國長公主 includes the rank 長公主 omitted by “Princess of Xu.”
為尼…號員明大師 is a Buddhist religious name, not a courtesy or style name.
許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), a different place from 徐州 Xuzhou.
Literal English also names 許州 as Xuzhou, conflating it with 徐州.
浴僕地 is 仆地, falling to the ground while bathing; 僕 is not “servant’s quarters.”
Literal English repeats the same misreading of 僕地 as servants’ quarters.
初入道, followed by the Daoist title 清虛靈照大師, is Daoist ordination, not Buddhist.
號清虛靈照大師 after 入道 is a religious name, not a style name.
袞國 is Gun; Yan would be 兗 or 燕.
Literal English likewise reads 袞國 as Yan.
附馬都尉 is 駙馬都尉, the commandant-escort / imperial son-in-law office, not a palace commissioner-in-ordinary.
二十九年 is a regnal year, not an elapsed span of twenty-nine years.
The title is 袞國大長公主 (Gun), not Yan.
Literal English also renders 袞國 as Yan.
十年夏 is a calendar year (tenth year, summer), not the princess’s tenth year of age; 年二十四 at death confirms the age reading is impossible here.
追封袞國 is Gun, not Yan.

decisions.after: When Shenzong took the throne, she was promoted to Senior Princess of Shu, redesignated Princess of Shu (Sichuan), and married Wang Shen, a general of the Left Guard.
decisions.reason: 舒國 and 蜀國 are successive distinct fiefs that both romanize as Shu; the proposed parenthetical Chinese characters are not English, so the second fief is marked as Sichuan Shu.
保聊 means remaining at ease; this sentence does not mention music (歌舞 follows only in the next sentence).
德寧 is Dening; Denning is a misspelling.
羈丱 is the bound-hair stage of childhood, not moral “restraint.”
滕妾 is the concubine (媵妾); the sentence does not establish 滕 as a surname.
康懿 is her first fief (始封康懿), not a posthumous name.
乞除開府 requests the kaifu privilege, not the office of Grand Preceptor (太師/太傅).
又為正夫求恩數 continues the princess’s actions; making the emperor the petitioner contradicts 上曰 refusing private grants.
開府之命 is the kaifu appointment, not Grand Preceptor of the Palace.

decisions.after: Roufu died in 1141; when the imperial coffin procession returned, her remains were brought back, interred, and she was posthumously made Senior Princess of the State of He.
decisions.reason: 和國長公主 omits the rank 長公主 in the original, but Grand Princess is 大長公主; the correct rank is Senior Princess.
四月 is a lunar month of Jingding 2, not the Gregorian month April.
娣姒 are brothers’ wives (sisters-in-law in the husband’s household), not the wife’s natal sisters.

claimRevisions.reason: The revised English distinguishes 舒國長公主 as Senior Princess of Shu from the later 蜀國 title.
The revised English distinguishes 蜀國 as Princess of Shu (Sichuan) from the earlier 舒國 title.
The accepted repair restores Dening for 德寧; the extracted English title was misspelled Denning.
The noble-title English value repeated the misspelling Denning for 德寧.

value.en: Senior Princess of the State of He

claimRevisions.reason: The revised English restores 長公主 as Senior Princess of the State of He, not merely Princess of He.

title.en: Senior Princess of the State of He

claimRevisions.reason: 和國長公主 is Senior Princess, not Grand Princess (大長公主); the posthumous-title English value must follow the revised rendering.
